name: Claire · gentle American
description: An adult woman speaking cultivated American English with a soft, velvety, rounded medium-low voice. Gentle warmth and a little storybook wonder, as though sharing a delightful discovery with one friend. A subtle smiling, whimsical lilt, with smooth flowing phrases and lightly softened consonants. Mellow rather than bright or piercing; tender and airy at the edges but fully voiced and intelligible, never whispering, squeaky, nasal, or childlike. Use naturally connected conversational speech: link each word's final sound gently into the next word, with fluid coarticulation and a continuous, easy breath through each thought. Lightly reduce unstressed little words and emphasize the meaning of the phrase, rather than giving every word a separate crisp attack or release. Smooth legato phrasing, with pauses at thought boundaries, not between individual words. Keep the words accurate and understandable. Keep a steady conversational reading pace of about 160 words per minute, with ordinary brief pauses. The playfulness is in the gentle melody of her voice, not in slower delivery or elongated words.

name: Grace · warm American
description: A mature adult woman speaking clear standard American English. Warm, mellow alto voice, soft spoken but fully audible, with a friendly conversational rhythm and gentle natural inflection. An attentive tutor explaining an interesting idea calmly to one person. Unhurried and articulate, without theatrical delivery or whispering.

name: Helen · refined American
description: An adult woman with a refined, lightly New England American English accent. Smooth medium-pitched voice, precise diction, and quiet warmth. Soft spoken, composed and thoughtful, with natural sentence emphasis and relaxed pauses. Conversational educational narration, not a newsreader, not breathy or whispered.
